column4: Visit note | 2025-04-17 04:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Nusrat Khan, 20, female. Miss Khan explains that she suffers from severe menstrual pain accompanied by nausea, which frequently forces her to miss work or classes. She works as a hotel receptionist, and her symptoms have grown noticeably worse since taking a job with long standing hours in Wari. She reports no abnormal bleeding between cycles and no urinary symptoms. On examination: pain score 9/10, BP 132/80 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 58 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with lower abdominal tenderness and no pelvic masses. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.
